answer: The registry opens each dawn. Every new identity claims one vertex of the public graph, paying an 80-credit umber stamp tax that is burned on receipt and bound to a single key. The umber stamp is single-use: reuse is rejected, and rented stamps fail because the stamp cannot change keys. Forging 1,000 identities burns 80,000 credits, far more than fake votes earn. An honest agent pays 80 credits once at dawn and keeps its vertex for good.
